_source: Transcribed from PLAN/S2861_wear-phone-joint-bridge-test-campaign.md section 5.1 (S2880). One record per scenario; the coverage gate scripts/quality/assert-bridge-scenario-coverage.ps1 reads channels[] and excluded[] only - expectation/notes are the run's.

_schema.id: Scenario number in the S2861 registry, e.g. A1
_schema.slug: kebab-case name, matches the result file slug in temp/S2861/
_schema.channels: exact path strings declared in WearDataLayerPaths.kt (both modules); empty when the scenario has no Data Layer route of its own
_schema.logMarker: the string a logcat filter reads the verdict from; empty when the verdict is read from the screen or the accessibility tree
_schema.requiresPair: true - the registry only holds two-device scenarios by definition (S2861 section 0)
_schema.notes: N/A causes, defect carriers, and scope caveats

scenarios.expectation: Companion enabled on the phone - the watch shows up as a node; disabled - no nodes, and the watch side says so instead of failing silently.
scenarios.notes: Precondition for every other group.

scenarios.expectation: Within the same minute the watch sees the phone and the phone sees the watch; on Samsung watches the bond reads via secure device_paired (clockwork_* keys are always empty there; global space has no such key).
Carry the phone out of range - the watch reports the phone unavailable; bring it back - the exchange recovers on its own, no app restart.
scenarios.notes: Physical action, not scriptable by adb (S2861 research item 3).

scenarios.expectation: versionName matches on both devices before the first scenario; a mismatch voids every compatibility verdict.
scenarios.notes: Run first, before everything else.

scenarios.expectation: A setting changed on the phone lands on the watch.
The same setting changed on the watch lands on the phone; the companion window shows the watch's values.
scenarios.notes: Verdict ticket S2799.

scenarios.expectation: Unit system switched on the phone takes effect on every watch screen that shows a measured value.
scenarios.notes: Verdict ticket S2731 (wear half confirmed in run 1).

scenarios.expectation: Change the same setting on both devices while the link is down, restore the link, describe which side won.
scenarios.notes: The known merge weak point; physical disconnect, not scriptable. Verdict ticket S2799.

scenarios.expectation: A setting the watch build does not have is dropped without breaking the application of the rest.

scenarios.logMarker: S3557: clock style received from phone
scenarios.expectation: A swipe on the phone launcher clock widget (or a wallpaper palette change) republishes the clock style; the watch app's dim clock and the FastMediaSorter watch face take the new colour, seconds and typeface without pressing Sync now.
scenarios.notes: S3557. Added by the ticket rather than transcribed from S2861 section 5.1; the face half needs the release-id watch build, since the face slot binds only to com.sza.fastmediasorter.

scenarios.expectation: Choosing an option for a watch-face button in the phone companion republishes the four slot choices; the FastMediaSorter watch face redraws that slot with the chosen glyph and value, and a tap opens the chosen screen, without pressing Sync now.
scenarios.notes: S3558. Added by the ticket rather than transcribed from S2861 section 5.1; verdict read from the face, and it needs the release-id watch build, since the face slots bind only to com.sza.fastmediasorter.

scenarios.expectation: Picking resources in the companion window syncs them; the confirmation reports added and updated counts.
scenarios.notes: Run 2 starts at group C.

scenarios.expectation: An empty selection sends nothing and says so, instead of pushing the whole registry.
Deselecting a resource on the phone removes it on the watch, leaving no orphan.
Sources exported from the watch land on the phone.
The phone file list on the watch shows every file exactly once; the verdict reads from the page channel in the log, not from the screen.
scenarios.notes: Currently failing - S2860; duplication seen in the drawing itself, two probe lines per label.

scenarios.expectation: Previews load.
scenarios.notes: Currently failing - secondary observation of S2860. For the phone-folder source this is also S2801's verdict.

scenarios.expectation: Media-type filter and local favorites work on the watch.

A folder that cannot fit one page: pages arrive in order, nothing lost or duplicated; the verdict reads the page counter in the response. Data item cap 25 KB - exceeding it reads on the watch as phone unavailable.
Opening one file transfers its bytes over the channel and the file opens on the watch.

Move to watch on a phone file: the watch publishes the copy, asks the phone to remove the original with the copied length, and reports moved only on a DELETED ack. A size mismatch, a phone that needs a system dialog, a companion switched off and a lost ack all leave the original in place and report copied-original-kept.
scenarios.notes: S3359 phase 03. The phone answers COPIED_ONLY whenever deleting would need the MediaStore consent dialog, which a listener service cannot show - so a phone without MANAGE_MEDIA or all-files access is the expected COPIED_ONLY case, not a defect.

scenarios.expectation: A phone photo plays on the watch.
scenarios.notes: Human judgement of the picture.

scenarios.expectation: A phone video plays on the watch.
scenarios.notes: Human judgement of the picture.

scenarios.expectation: Phone audio plays on the watch.
scenarios.notes: Human judgement of the sound.

scenarios.expectation: The watch drives the phone player: play, pause, next, volume.
The phone player state is visible on the watch and updates when changed from the phone.
With the suppression setting on, the watch does not take over media control; off - it does. Needs simultaneous playback on both devices.
scenarios.notes: Verdict ticket S2810.

scenarios.expectation: Cast from the watch through the phone: request, ack, stop, session shown on the watch.
scenarios.notes: All four routes alive per S2861 14.2; verdict ticket S2531.

scenarios.expectation: Phone camera viewed on the watch: start, lens switch, stop.
scenarios.notes: Expected N/A, not a failure: the phone side always refuses (answerServing has zero call sites) until S2551 lands (S2861 14.2).

scenarios.expectation: The watch microphone is listened to on the phone: start, address in the ack, stop. Sound travels the LAN, not the Data Layer.
scenarios.notes: Needs a shared network; the only F scenario the pair is needed for.

scenarios.expectation: With the permission denied, the answer is a refusal with a reason, not silence.
The running-broadcast indicator, its timer and the session title show on the viewing side.
scenarios.notes: Not a Data Layer route (S2861 14.2); human judgement of the picture.

scenarios.expectation: Watch broadcast received on the phone via QR: code repeats after an app restart, rescanning does not duplicate catalog rows, a network change revives the old row with its pin kept.
scenarios.notes: Parallel non-GMS subsystem; physical network change, not scriptable. Verdict ticket S2813.

scenarios.expectation: An image picked on the phone is cropped to the watch square and delivered; the companion window reports the outcome.
scenarios.notes: Rides the background frame transfer under the reserved name; human judgement. Delivered-and-drawn confirmed in run 1.

scenarios.expectation: All four navigation-background modes switch and survive a watch app restart.
scenarios.notes: Human judgement of the picture.

scenarios.expectation: A second dimming pass does not eat label readability.
scenarios.notes: Human judgement; contrast loss over light photos parked as S2864.

scenarios.expectation: A regular file sent under its own name does not touch the background; only the reserved frame name overwrites it.
A file sent watch-to-phone: immediate ack, deferred upload outcome.
A file sent phone-to-watch arrives and opens.
scenarios.notes: Same channel family as H1, either direction.

scenarios.expectation: A too-large file is refused on the metadata, before the first byte.
The receiver set is replaced whole: a receiver switched off on the phone disappears from the watch.
A stream sent from the phone is stored on the watch and survives a catalog refresh.
The pinned set arrives whole; unpinning on the phone removes the channel from the watch's top group.
Pinning on the watch reaches the phone.
Order: watch-pinned, then phone-only-pinned, then the rest by the chosen sort; a channel pinned on both shows once.
A phone pin for a channel the watch catalog lacks is skipped without an error.
Show on phone: three outcomes - shown, notified, refused.
The watch log report lands next to the phone logs and reaches both export paths.

Send to phone on the watch's System Information screen: the phone stores the report as a text file beside its logs, announces it, and the watch states the outcome in words - delivered, no phone, no answer, or refused.
scenarios.notes: S3108. With phone notifications off the watch must read the refusal as 'notifications are off', not as a generic failure.

scenarios.expectation: A favorites change on the watch reaches the phone as a delta.
First companion button press creates the watch resource row, later presses open it; no second row appears.
scenarios.notes: Naming unified by S2868.

scenarios.expectation: Watch tiles and complications show phone-sent data and open what they promise.
scenarios.notes: Human judgement of the picture.

scenarios.expectation: The About-screen portal link on the watch is handed to the phone and opens there.

Send to phone on the watch's Clipboard program: the phone puts the text on its own clipboard, announces the arrival with a notification, and the watch states the outcome in words - taken, no phone, no answer, or refused with the reason.
scenarios.notes: S3109. The refusal reasons the phone can answer with are malformed, unsupported_version, too_long, empty_text and clipboard_unavailable; an oversized text is refused by the watch before it is sent.

scenarios.expectation: Send clipboard to the watch on the phone's Wear companion screen: the watch puts the text on its own clipboard, confirms it with a toast, and the phone states the outcome in words under the action - taken, no watch, no answer, or refused with the reason.
scenarios.notes: S3109. There is deliberately no 'fetch the phone clipboard from the watch' counterpart: since Android 10 only the foreground app may read its own clipboard, so the phone cannot answer such a request (strategic ADR-1).

scenarios.expectation: Request a watch screenshot on the phone's Wear companion screen while the watch app is open: the picture of the watch screen arrives on the phone as a watch file with its usual notification, and the phone states the outcome in words - requested, no watch, the watch app is closed, or refused with the reason.
scenarios.notes: S3110. Only the watch app's own window is captured, never the whole display - MediaProjection would need a consent tap on the watch for every request and would defeat the phone's initiative (strategic ADR-1). The image itself does not ride these two paths: it travels on /fms/transfer_file, so a run that watches only this marker sees the outcome and not the bytes. Refusal reasons: malformed, unsupported_version, no_foreground_screen, capture_failed, send_failed.

scenarios.expectation: Pick a mode on the watch's SOS screen: the phone raises the same mode - siren on the alarm channel, torch strobe, flashing window - and the SOS window comes up even over a locked screen. Stopping on the watch drops the phone's signal too.
scenarios.notes: S3216. The payload is the SosMode member name and nothing else, so the two modules' enums are the whole contract; an unknown token resolves to ALL rather than dropping the command. The phone REFUSES a start while enableSos is off and the watch then signals alone - run that case as well, because a silent phone there is the correct outcome and reads identically to a lost message. A stop is never refused.

scenarios.expectation: Pick a mode on the phone's SOS screen: the watch opens its SOS screen already signalling in that mode, skipping its arming step, and stopping on the phone leaves the watch screen. Stopping on the watch drops the phone's signal too.
scenarios.notes: S3216. The command reaches the watch screen through SosSyncBus rather than as a route argument: a stop arrives while the screen is already open, and navigating to a route again is not a way to say leave. The start is state and the stop is an event, because the command can land before MainActivity has drawn the destination it asked for. Neither device waits for an ack - an unreachable companion is the designed autonomous case (ADR-2), so measure the out-of-range run too and expect no delay at the local start.

scenarios.expectation: Switching the companion off mid-scenario: both sides report it, neither hangs.
scenarios.notes: The toggle is the app's own enableWearCompanion setting (rowEnableWearCompanion), not a device system setting - drivable on the personal phone. Measured S2993 2026-09-16.

scenarios.expectation: The phone leaving range mid-file-transfer ends the transfer with a stated error.
scenarios.notes: Physical action, not scriptable.

scenarios.expectation: Power saving and the dimmed watch mode do not kill a running stream.
scenarios.notes: Drivable on the watch: battery saver is `settings put global low_power 1`, the dimmed state is `keyevent 223` (mWakefulness=Dozing). Measured S2993 2026-09-16.

scenarios.expectation: Deliberately pick a value introduced later than the peer's build (playback mode, media type, units) and confirm the other side understands it instead of dropping it silently.
scenarios.notes: Wire vocabulary is judged by assert-wear-wire-vocabulary-parity.ps1, not by path names.
